title: Developer Experience Documentation Playbook — SDKs, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Docs Ops
author: Claire Zhang
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook defines standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues with fixes. The goal is to make docs consistent, discoverable, and reliable for internal teams and external users.

Scope
- All public-facing SDK guides (Python, JavaScript, Go, Java).
- Quickstarts and deployable templates (starter apps, server + client examples).
- API examples and canonical snippets for the REST and SDK surfaces.
- Docs site operating procedures (publishing, rollouts, monitoring).
- Top support issues and canonical fixes maintained by DevEx and Support.

Roles & Ownership
- Owner: DevEx Documentation (team in engineering) — primary contact: Claire Zhang.
- Reviewers: API Platform (Marcus Lee), SDK Maintainers (Priya Nambiar), Support (Ethan Park).
- Escalation: If docs content impacts SLA or security, escalate to Product and Security via #doc-escalations.

Standards & Style
- Tone: technical, concise, example-first. Avoid narrative design docs here.
- Structure: each guide must include: short intro, quickstart example, installation, minimal example, advanced usage, troubleshooting, API reference links, and changelog.
- Naming: filenames and page titles use short-dash-case (e.g., python-sdk-quickstart-2026).
- Code: all code snippets must be runnable and pinned to a tag/commit on GitHub (see Templates section).
- Versioning: include a top-level "SDK version tested" badge with semver and build id.

Templates & Required Sections (checklist)
Every new document must include the following sections in order:
1) Title and one-line summary.
2) Audience / prerequisites (OS, Python/Node version, cloud region if relevant).
3) Quickstart (5–10 lines) with copy-paste runnable example.
4) Installation / setup commands.
5) Minimal API example and expected output.
6) Configuration options & security notes (API keys, scopes, KMS).
7) Troubleshooting / known issues.
8) Links to related pages and SDK repo with commit hash.
9) Maintainers and last updated date.

Example Quickstart Template (Python)
---
# Quickstart: Python (copy/paste)
1. Install the package
```bash
pip install redwood-inference-sdk==0.12.3
```
2. Environment variable (recommended)
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-••••••••
```
3. Minimal example
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.generate(text="Write a 2-line product elevator pitch for Redwood Inference")
print(resp.text)
```
Expected output (truncated):
"Redwood Inference provides a high-performance, developer-first platform for running LLM inference with predictable latency and cost."
---
(When adding other SDKs, match the same structure; ensure the example runs in CI.)

API Examples & Canonical Snippets
- Provide both REST and SDK examples for each common pattern: text generation, chat, streaming, embeddings, and function/tool calling.
- Use consistent input prompts and example responses so tests can assert outputs in docs CI.
- Include curl examples for quick reproducibility. Example: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0", "input":"Summarize the following text in one sentence: ..."}'
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures
1) Branching & Publishing
  - Author creates a docs branch in the docs repo: docs/<ticket-id>-<short-title>.
  - Draft pages use status: draft and must include the reviewers list.
  - When ready, open a PR against main/docs-site. Include "docs: <short summary>" in PR title and request at least 2 reviewers (DevEx + SDK owner).
2) CI checks
  - Linting (markdown/style), runnable-snippets check, dead-link detection, and API example snapshot tests must pass.
  - The docs CI uses the tag docs-ci:v3; failures block merge.
3) Release window
  - Docs merges are continuous; however breaking API changes must follow the product release calendar and include two-week notice.
4) Post-publish validation
  - Within 24 hours of merge, validate live quickstarts for each SDK using the docs smoke test job: `ci/docs-smoke-test`. Failure triggers rollback and a ticket in backlog.

Top Support Issues (canonical fixes)
- Issue: SDK authentication errors (401)
  - Symptom: "Unauthorized" when calling client.generate().
  - Canonical fix: Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY is set and has correct scope; rotate key and update environment; ensure local proxy (if any) passes Authorization header.
  - Owner: Support -> escalates to SDK team if library bug.
- Issue: Streaming responses truncated
  - Symptom: Partial content and connection closed early.
  - Canonical fix: Check client library streaming settings (timeout, chunk_size), confirm server-side SLOs; reproduce with curl to isolate client vs network. If reproducible with curl, file incident (see Incident Process).
- Issue: Embeddings quality regressions
  - Symptom: Retrieval experiments show lower recall after model rollout.
  - Canonical fix: Roll back to prior model variant via routing policy, run evaluation harness (applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness) and open regression triage ticket with model-onboarding.

Monitoring & Metrics for Docs Health
- Key metrics tracked weekly: docs CI pass rate, number of runnable-snippet failures, number of doc-related support tickets opened, average time to update quickstarts after API changes.
- Targets: maintain docs CI pass rate >= 98% and mean time to update quickstarts <= 7 days for non-breaking changes.

Maintenance Cadence
- Monthly: Docs triage meeting (DevEx + SDK leads + Support) to review open doc tickets, flaky examples, and required updates for upcoming releases.
- Quarterly: Audit top 20 quickstarts and API examples for accuracy and runtime with the smoke-test harness.

Operational Playbooks (short)
- Rapid rollback: If a docs change introduces a production-breaking example that causes customer outages, revert the merge and open an incident in PagerDuty with tag `docs-regression`.
- Security-sensitive changes: All docs that reference KMS/HSM or customer data handling must be reviewed by Security before publishing.

Maintenance templates (copyable)
- New SDK Guide Checklist:
  - [ ] Title and summary
  - [ ] Quickstart example (runnable)
  - [ ] Installation steps with pinned versions
  - [ ] API example and expected response
  - [ ] Troubleshooting / known issues
  - [ ] Link to SDK repo with commit hash
  - [ ] Reviewers assigned

Appendix: Useful Commands & Links
- Docs CI: `ci/docs-runner --branch $BRANCH`
- Smoke test job: `ci/docs-smoke-test`
- API reference: https://api.redwood.ai/docs (canonical)
- SDK repos: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python (pin to commit)
- Incident runbook (oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks)
